rv.q: But what keeps it from being pretentious is the sincere explosive joy with which it’s constructed.
You’re never going to see a finer revival of “Travesties,” so catch this one while you can.
What emerges from the churning wash of “Travesties” is one of the sweetest, sauciest and strangest defenses of art ever to land on a stage.

Tom Hollander gives a tour de force performance as Henry Carr, the elderly British consul who serves as narrator and unreliable witness to the wild artistic ferment that was Zurich during World War I.
Tom Hollander's performance as Henry Carr is a marvel of precision and comic timing, anchoring this brilliant revival
Sparkling and incisive revival...continues to illuminate our untethered times with whiplash accuracy.
Tom Hollander's performance as Henry Carr is a tour de force of comic timing and intellectual agility, anchoring this revival of Stoppard's brilliant play about art, politics, and memory.

"Under Patrick Marber’s tirelessly inventive direction, a cast featuring the inspired Tom Hollander in the pivotal role provides a sparkling return to Stoppard’s revolutionary carnival of Zurich in 1917...Along for the ride, too, is Tristan Tzara, one of the founders of the dada anti-art movement and here played to florid perfection by Seth Numrich.
Mr. Stoppard's play remains a glittering intellectual entertainment.
The facets of Stoppard's jewellike play are overwhelmingly, even ostentatiously brilliant.
You may miss a plot point here or a reference there, but you can count on a belly laugh waiting around the corner.

What pertains here, however, is: No matter by what definition of art you swear, this Travesties—thanks to Stoppard, Hollander, Marber, and everyone connected to it—is that rare thing: Art with a capital “A.”
Tom Stoppard's brilliant, bewildering and ultimately bewitching Travesties is back on Broadway in a production that crackles with wit and intelligence.
It may be nonsense, but at least it’s clever nonsense.
Even if you can't solve it all as you watch, it's a pleasure to engage with a production that does Travesties full justice.
Bravo to this fine actor who New Yorkers have seen only on screen and Director Marber for giving us not just another revival, but a decidedly fresh and enjoyable one.

"'Travesties,' a nonstop tourney of wit and erudition, has often been called a brainteaser, but brain tickler comes so much closer to the jubilant staging...This 'Travesties' belongs first and foremost to Hollander...

Luckily, the first Broadway revival of Stoppard’s 1974 play turns this challenging exercise in virtuosity into an often-hilarious entertainment, with lively direction by Patrick Marber and a spot-on eight-member cast led by the terrific Tom Hollander.
Only a playwright as brilliantly inventive as Stoppard could put all that together to come up with an uproarious work that seriously questions the nature of art.
It may be nonsense, but at least it is clever nonsense.
Stoppard’s genius, especially in his earlier work, is to mix high intellect with low comedy, and Travesties manages to be both deeply thoughtful and guffawingly funny.
The happy bonus of the brightly acted Roundabout production at the Theater is how often the 1974 comedy engages one's smile muscles.
For what it's worth, you have my blessing to rest your mind at various intervals, because no matter where you rejoin, there will be some bit of awesome insanity to keep your head in an endless spin.
The drama becomes blunted when it feels as if we are being shouted at; the stage of the Lucille Lortel feels too small for it.
But all things considered, it is hard to imagine a better production of it coming along anytime soon, and how do you get to complain about a play being too smart?
But these multi-talented thespians do it with such zesty effortlessness, they make it all seem like so much fun.
Arguably the best and smartest play on Broadway right now, and a must see for any serious theatregoer.
The cast magnificently delivers the bite in the sarcasm and the punch in the irony.
In fact, most of “Travesties” will leave you with a wide grin on your mouth, while still providing fodder for your brain.
What Marber and company have pulled off, however, makes a travesty of my reservations.
Dizzying and dazzling, this superb Stoppard revival from director Patrick Marber zips along.
This is still one of the playwright's most impressive achievements.
The most pleasantly surprising revival this season...Patrick Marber and his extraordinary cast have managed to strike comedy gold.
It's a miraculous invention of finely tuned dynamics and impossible fun.
I did not expect to be so delighted by this rollicking production.
However, I didn’t care because the tremendously talented Tom Hollander plays Henry Carr and he is amazing!
One walks away from Travesties not full of empty calories, but exhausted and happily challenged and entertained.
Tom Hollander and company do a superb job of a play that does not easily give up its secrets.
A rollicking good time with an intellectual perspective wrapped in theater of the absurd.
For the discerning theatre-goer it is a must-have ticket.
Travesties demands attention from its audience as it challenges our intellect -- but it moves quickly and intelligently so there’s no dozing off.
But stay alert and the charming company will guide you through an evening that can tickle your intellect as well as your funny bone.
